A is better because it names the specific failure that 8px gaps are smaller than 24px padding and sets group gaps to 24–32px, while B only calls 8px tight and defaults to a 16px gap that merely matches its reduced padding. A also removes the inner card chrome and calls out the 48px stacked padding, which more directly lightens the panel. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B names the 8px-versus-24px gap problem, flattens the inner surfaces, and gives CSS a developer can apply. A also flattens one nesting level, drops doubled edges, and sets heading space to 32px above and 12px below, but it never states that the gaps are smaller than the padding, and its scale sets card padding and card gaps both to 16px. Both answers are practical; B matches every rubric item more tightly.

passes.notes: Both answers flatten the nested cards, cut doubled borders and shadows, and attach headings with more space above than below, using concrete values.
